acceptance_criteria.source: "Reject symlinks in every destination path component."
acceptance_criteria.text: A scaffold write into the cached GitOps checkout is refused when the destination's final file or any parent directory component is a symlink.

acceptance_criteria.source: "Verify resolved parent paths remain beneath the repository root."
acceptance_criteria.text: Before a scaffold write, the resolved parent path of the destination is verified to remain beneath the cached repository root.

acceptance_criteria.source: "Open files using no-follow semantics where supported."
acceptance_criteria.text: The final open of a scaffold destination file uses no-follow semantics where the platform supports it.

acceptance_criteria.source: "Add tests for final-file and parent-directory symlinks."
acceptance_criteria.text: Tests exist covering a symlink as the final destination file and a symlink in a parent directory of the destination.

acceptance_criteria.source: "Read remote.origin.url whenever opening the cache. Compare it to the requested repository identity. Fail closed or recreate the cache on mismatch."
acceptance_criteria.text: When an existing cached GitOps checkout is opened, its remote.origin.url is read and compared to the configured repository identity, and on mismatch the operation fails closed or the cache is recreated.

acceptance_criteria.source: "Before pushing, resolve and report the destination URL."
acceptance_criteria.text: Before pushing to the GitOps repository, the effective push destination URL is resolved and reported to the user.

acceptance_criteria.source: "Disable hooks for commits in the CLI-owned cache, for example through an isolated Git configuration."
acceptance_criteria.text: Git hooks are disabled for commits the CLI makes in the CLI-owned GitOps cache.

acceptance_criteria.source: "Disable unexpected signing and interactive prompting." (signing choice was left to the assistant and is not encoded)
acceptance_criteria.text: Interactive prompting is disabled for the git invocations the CLI runs in the cache.

acceptance_criteria.source: "Verify the staged path list immediately before committing."
acceptance_criteria.text: Immediately before committing in the GitOps cache, the staged path list is verified to be exactly the expected set and the commit is refused otherwise.

acceptance_criteria.source: "Verify the resulting commit's changed paths before pushing. Abort if the commit contains anything outside the expected set."
acceptance_criteria.text: Before pushing, the resulting commit's changed paths are verified and the push is aborted if the commit contains anything outside the expected set.

acceptance_criteria.source: "Preserve the effective port in repository identity comparison."
acceptance_criteria.text: Repository identity comparison preserves the effective port, so https://git.example.com:8443/org/repo and https://git.example.com:9443/org/repo compare as different repositories.

acceptance_criteria.source: "hardening should be scoped to CLI-managed GitOps checkouts."
acceptance_criteria.text: Hook hardening (hook disabling and --no-verify) applies only to CLI-managed GitOps checkouts, not to every git client.

acceptance_criteria.source: "User source-repository pushes should retain their normal hook policy."
acceptance_criteria.text: Pushes from user source repositories (e.g. release tag creation) run the user's normal git hooks.

acceptance_criteria.source: "For managed GitOps checkouts, fail closed when the effective push URL does not identify the configured repository. Alternatively, remove an unexpected repository-local pushurl and revalidate before pushing."
acceptance_criteria.text: For a managed GitOps checkout, when the effective push URL (via remote.origin.pushurl or url.*.pushInsteadOf) does not identify the configured repository, the push does not proceed: either the operation fails closed, or an unexpected repository-local pushurl is removed and the destination revalidated before pushing.

acceptance_criteria.source: "Any intentional redirect should require explicit configuration rather than a warning."
acceptance_criteria.text: An intentional push redirect for a managed GitOps checkout requires explicit configuration; a mismatch is never merely warned about.

acceptance_criteria.source: "These all pass: go test ./internal/deploy ./internal/git ./internal/gitops / go test ./internal/release ./internal/source / go vet ./internal/deploy ./internal/git ./internal/gitops ./internal/release ./internal/source"
acceptance_criteria.text: The repository's checks pass: go test ./internal/deploy ./internal/git ./internal/gitops; go test ./internal/release ./internal/source; go vet ./internal/deploy ./internal/git ./internal/gitops ./internal/release ./internal/source.

acceptance_criteria.source: Implementing fixes across internal/deploy, internal/git and internal/gitops implies the project still builds and nothing unrelated breaks.
acceptance_criteria.text: The repository's checks pass: go build ./... and go test ./... (the existing suite is not broken by the changes).

analysis.task_statement: Implement fixes in a Go CLI (intropy-cli) for three P1 git-safety findings: (1) scaffold writes in internal/deploy must not escape the cached GitOps checkout via symlinks in the leaf or any parent path component; (2) an existing cached GitOps checkout's remote.origin.url must be verified against the configured repository identity before fetch/push, failing closed or re-cloning on mismatch, and the push destination reported/verified; (3) git hooks must not be able to widen an exact-path commit in the CLI-managed cache, with staged and committed path sets verified before commit and push. Follow-up review turns tightened the fixes: repository identity must preserve non-default ports, hook disabling must be scoped to CLI-managed GitOps checkouts only (user source-repo pushes keep hooks), and a mismatched effective push URL (pushurl / pushInsteadOf) must fail closed rather than merely print a note. Tests required for each.

turn_script.intent: Two review blockers on the implemented fixes: (a) repository identity comparison must preserve the effective port so URLs differing only in port compare as different repositories; (b) hook hardening (disabling hooks, --no-verify on push) must be scoped to CLI-managed GitOps checkouts only — pushes from user source repositories (e.g. release tag creation) must retain their normal hook policy. Keep the exact-commit protections (hooks disabled in managed cache, staged paths checked before commit, committed paths checked before push).
